Baseline milestone and baseline studies Monthly progress project reports.Agriculture KAP studies Monitoring reports Technical reports800 individuals in Deir ez Zor and 500 individuals in Rural Damascus

In our intervention we successfully achieved gender parity in the engagement of mediators negotiators and technical experts with women comprising 50 of these roles. This is particularly noteworthy given the critical influence these positions have on the planning implementation and outcomes of our project activities. This result is partly attributed to the gender dynamics in the civil society sector in Moldova which tends to be dominated by women. Their active participation has contributed to the inclusiveness and effectiveness of our project interventions.

comment.narrative: Yes during the evaluation it was observed that project targeted women and girls empowerment at two levels i.e. CSOs and community level.Our approach to womens empowerment was multifaceted and extended beyond individual beneficiaries to encompass organizational and systemic levels. The project actively prioritized partnerships with CSOs led by women. This not only fostered a gendersensitive approach to service delivery but also positioned women as leaders and decisionmakers in the projects implementation. The project also included a strong capacitybuilding component. We provided training on leadership and other key skills to women leading CSOs. Their enhanced skills and competencies will continue to be an asset to their communities beyond the life of this project. Further we ensured that the CSOs we partnered with integrated a gender perspective into their activities. This helped to ensure that services were not just accessible to women and girls but were also sensitive to their specific needs and experiences. Lastly in the communities HHs headed by women old age and disable women were targeted to provide the assistance.

comment.narrative: Global Peace Index data increase or remain stable in 2023.

According to GPI 2022 Moldova ranking in GPI was 62 and in 2023 a positive change was observed in ranking as 57 with a change score of 0.008. Moldova experienced a slight improvement in overall peacefulness owing to improvements in violent demonstrations and perceptions of criminality. Despite the overall score improving Moldovas political stability deteriorated by 4.2 per cent in 2022. Russias invasion on Ukraine has escalated regional instability and increased the threat of a broader conflict between Russia and the NATO alliance partners. The Russias war over Ukraine and the resultant sanctions imposed on Russia also brought major economic disruptions including strong increases in staple commodity prices. The worsening economic conditions domestically stirred public pressure on the government to mitigate the negative impacts on living conditions. The conflict has resulted in an unprecedented influx of refugees from Ukraine further straining Moldovas limited resources. The fighting threatened to spread to Moldovas Russianbacked breakaway region Transnistria.

comment.narrative: Since the end of 2021 Moldovas population is being hardly hit by a string of crises. As a retaliatory measure to Moldovas decision to reduce its dependency on Russian gas supplies Moscow increased the price of the gas it supplies to Moldova by practically four times from November 2021. This renders it hardly accessible for a vast portion of the population of Moldova the poorest in Europe and many households were led to stop using gas altogether in winter times for the lack of resources or to drastically reduce expenses for other basic needs.Since February 2022 the invasion of Ukraine by Russia also brought additional challenges to Moldovans as hundreds of thousands of Ukrainian refugees enter the country. While most only transit through Moldova as of end of April 2022 still an estimated 100000 refugees remain in the country by choice or necessity. Moldovans already vulnerable by all means are rising to the task of welcoming them within their homes sharing their meager resources but they are increasingly struggling to bear this additional burden.To top it all the Russian invasion additionally sparked global spikes in the prices of basic commodities leading to galloping inflation worldwide. In Moldova the inflation rate mounted to over 16 as of January 2022. Heavily reliant on imports at practically all levels Moldova has had to suspend its exports from wartorn Ukraine one of if not its main supplier as a result of war and turn towards European markets in particular Romania where prices are higher. The action was designed to limit the negative socioeconomic impact of the energy crisis but meanwhile also contributed in preventing a significant deterioration of the situation and the development of a humanitarian crisis among the Moldovan population as a result of Russian invasion to Ukraine. As a result the action contributed to the response towards both emerging crises that occur recently in Moldova by releasing timely cash support to 36 815 vulnerable households.

This renders it hardly accessible for a vast portion of the population of Moldova the poorest in Europe and many households were led to stop using gas altogether in winter times for the lack of resources or to drastically reduce expenses for other basic needs.Since February 2022 the invasion of Ukraine by Russia also brought additional challenges to Moldovans as hundreds of thousands of Ukrainian refugees enter the country. While most only transit through Moldova as of end of April 2022 still an estimated 100000 refugees remain in the country by choice or necessity. Moldovans already vulnerable by all means are rising to the task of welcoming them within their homes sharing their meager resources but they are increasingly struggling to bear this additional burden.To top it all the Russian invasion additionally sparked global spikes in the prices of basic commodities leading to galloping inflation worldwide. In Moldova the inflation rate mounted to over 16 as of January 2022. Heavily reliant on imports at practically all levels Moldova has had to suspend its exports from wartorn Ukraine one of if not its main supplier as a result of war and turn towards European markets in particular Romania where prices are higher. The action was designed to limit the negative socioeconomic impact of the energy crisis but meanwhile also contributed in preventing a significant deterioration of the situation and the development of a humanitarian crisis among the Moldovan population as a result of Russian invasion to Ukraine. As a result the action contributed to the response towards both emerging crises that occur recently in Moldova by releasing timely cash support to 36 815 vulnerable households.

title.narrative: Oc.1.2 % of vulnerable population with access to essential heating material

description.narrative: This indicator will be measured through PDM and if possible during the baseline as well to know about the beneficiaries access to essential heating material prior to receiving the assistance. A comparison would allow to understand that how many targeted beneficiaries have better access to heating material as a result of project intervention. Access to heating material will be measured through the general affordability and availability of heating material in the market. Affordability will be measured through the individuals ability to buy wood or other heating materials from the market and availability is referred to the overall uninterrupted supply in the market.

comment.narrative: X of targeted households who have increased their level of access to heating material.

Methodology The methodology used for calculating the indicator related to access to essential heating materials was based on two primary components each carrying equal weightage of 50 Affordability C1 This component assessed the extent to which People in Need PIN financial assistance enabled vulnerable households to cover the gap in their heating costs or access to heating materials during the winter season. Question Q1 used for collecting data on C1 To what extent the support of People in Need PIN in the form of cash financial assistance enable you to cover gap in your needs related to heating costs or heating materials that you were not able to cover by your own means during winter season of 20222023 Since the baseline data was collected before we offered any support the Q1 was modified into To what extent the social assistance compensation or inkind support enable you to cover gap in your needs related to heating costs or heating materials that you were not able to cover by your own means during winter season 20212022 Availability C2 This component aimed to determine if there were any instances during the same period when heating materials supply such as gas or other options like wood and coal were interrupted or unavailable in the local market. Question Q2 used for collecting data on C2 Was there time when heating materials supply was interrupted e.g. gas or not available in the local market e.g. wood coal The respondents answers to both questions were used to calculate the indicator value for each target group total male and female to gauge difference in their access to essential heating materials. Comparison of Baseline and PDMs results The results from the second round of cash distribution Output 1Phase 2 displayed significant improvements in the percentage of vulnerable households with increased access to essential heating materials. The beneficiaries of the second round of cash assistance demonstrated improved access to heating materials which is manifested with a notable increase in the overall indicator value as reported by 653 of the targeted households this indicates a commendable achievement that surpass the 60 as set for the target see percentage change and composition between baseline and PDMPhase 2 Round 2 below Total 17.5 percentage points Female 15.3 percentage points Male 18.0 percentage points Moreover the comparison between the results of the first round of cash assistance Phase 1 20212023 and the second round Phase 2 20222023 in regard to access to essential heating materials demonstrates significant improvements. The results clearly highlight the progress made that could be observed when comparing both rounds and the improvements in the indicator values for total female and male target groups indicate a successful implementation of interventions targeting vulnerable households. Findings and Conclusions The results of the second round of cash assistance vide Phase 2 exceed those of the first round indicating effectiveness of continuous assistance Phase 2 vide beneficiaries supported with five monthly payments versus oneoff assistance provided during first round Phase 1 beneficiaries supported one time. As assessed the efforts made in addressing affordability seem to have been effective in driving these improvements particularly with application of modality alike during Phase 2. Moreover the cash interventions contributed to the positive change in the indicator value as evidenced by the higher percentage of vulnerable households gaining access to heating materials. By providing cash financial assistance to bridge the gap in heating costs the intervention has evidently addressed the key barriers faced by the vulnerable population.

comment.narrative: Target of at least 12.

Within the project 4 different FSTP schemes were organized by PIN. Under FSTP 1 five local CSOs providing hot meals through social canteens located in Bali Cahul Vulcaneti Edine Glodeni were supported and the support was later extended until March 2023. Under FSTP 2 another ten CSOs vide CSOs from Anenii Noi Caueni Cahul Chisinau Basarabeasca Bali Soroca Telenesti Criuleni and Dorchia were supported to provide necessary services such as e.g. wood coal foodhygienic products psychological counseling etc. to the most vulnerable population. Further under FSTP 3 a media organization was supported to monitor distribution of the aid under the project and lastly under FSTP 4 an environmental CSO was selected to advocate on energy efficiency measures.
